agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

--- # goimports-reviser ![logo](./images/reviser-muscot_200.png) Tool for Golang to sort goimports by 3-4 groups: std, general, company (optional), and project dependencies. Also formats your code (no need to use `gofmt` or `goimports` separately). ## Features - Sort imports into logical groups (stdlib, general, company, project) - Remove unused imports with `-rm-unused` - Set aliases for versioned packages with `-set-alias` - Format code automatically with `-format` - Apply to directories recursively - Group company imports separately with `-company-prefixes` ## Usage ### Basic command: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./reviser/reviser.go ``` ### Apply to a directory recursively: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format -recursive reviser ``` ### Apply to all files: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./... ``` ### Apply to multiple targets: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./reviser/reviser.go ./pkg/... ``` ### Options: ```text Usage of goimports-reviser: -apply-to-generated-files Apply imports sorting and formatting(if the option is set) to generated files. Generated file is a file with first comment which starts with comment '// Code generated'. Optional parameter. -company-prefixes string Company package prefixes which will be placed after 3rd-party group by default(if defined). Values should be comma-separated. Optional parameters. -excludes string Exclude files or dirs, example: '.git/,proto/*.go'. -file-path string Deprecated. Put file name as an argument(last item) of command line. -format Option will perform additional formatting. Optional parameter. -imports-order string Your imports groups can be sorted in your way. std - std import group; general - libs for general purpose; company - inter-org or your company libs(if you set '-company-prefixes'-option, then 4th group will be split separately. In other case, it will be the part of general purpose libs); project - your local project dependencies; blanked - imports with "_" alias; dotted - imports with "." alias. Optional parameter. (default "std,general,company,project") -list-diff Option will list files whose formatting differs from goimports-reviser. Optional parameter. -local string Deprecated -output string Can be "file", "write" or "stdout". Whether to write the formatted content back to the file or to stdout. When "write" together with "-list-diff" will list the file name and write back to the file. Optional parameter. (default "file") -project-name string Your project name(ex.: github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser). Optional parameter. -recursive Apply rules recursively if target is a directory. In case of ./... execution will be recursively applied by default. Optional parameter. -rm-unused Remove unused imports. Optional parameter. -separate-named Separate named imports from their group with a new line. Optional parameter. -set-alias Set alias for versioned package names, like 'github.com/go-pg/pg/v9'. In this case import will be set as 'pg "github.com/go-pg/pg/v9"'. Optional parameter. -set-exit-status set the exit status to 1 if a change is needed/made. Optional parameter. -use-cache Use cache to improve performance. Optional parameter. -version Show version. ``` ## Examples ### Before usage: ```go package testdata import ( "log" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/testdata/innderpkg" "bytes" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" ) ``` ### After usage: ```go package testdata import ( "bytes" "log" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/testdata/innderpkg" ) ``` Comments for imports are preserved: ```go package testdata import ( "fmt" // comments to the package here ) ``` ### Example with `-company-prefixes` option Before: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" //fmt package "golang.org/x/exp/slices" //custom package "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" // this is a company package which is not a part of the project, but is a part of your organization "goimports-reviser/pkg" ) ``` After: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" // fmt package "golang.org/x/exp/slices" // custom package "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" // this is a company package which is not a part of the project, but is a part of your organization "goimports-reviser/pkg" ) ``` ### Example with `-imports-order std,general,company,project,blanked,dotted` option Before: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( _ "github.com/pkg1" . "github.com/pkg2" "fmt" //fmt package "golang.org/x/exp/slices" //custom package "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" // this is a company package which is not a part of the project, but is a part of your organization "goimports-reviser/pkg" ) ``` After: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" // fmt package "golang.org/x/exp/slices" // custom package "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" // this is a company package which is not a part of the project, but is a part of your organization "goimports-reviser/pkg" _ "github.com/pkg1" . "github.com/pkg2" ) ``` ### Example with `-format` option Before: ```go package main func test(){ } func additionalTest(){ } ``` After: ```go package main func test(){ } func additionalTest(){ } ``` ### Example with `-separate-named` option Before: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" extpkg "google.com/golang/pkg" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" extslice "github.com/PeterRK/slices" ) ``` After: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" extpkg "google.com/golang/pkg" extslice "github.com/PeterRK/slices" ) ```

```
rm -rf /tmp/t
cd /workspace
cat > main.go <<'MAINEOF'
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"

	"goimports-reviser/reviser"
)

// version info
var (
	Version = "3.0.0-20260303205914-9926ea38658f"
	Tag     = "v3.0.0-20260303205914-9926ea38658f"
	Commit  = "n/a"
	Source  = "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/v3"
	GoVer   = "go1.26.0"
)

var (
	fShowVersion      bool
	fShowVersionOnly  bool
	fProjectName      string
	fCompanyPrefixes  string
	fOutput           string
	fRemoveUnused     bool
	fSetAlias         bool
	fFormat           bool
	fRecursive        bool
	fListDiff         bool
	fSetExitStatus    bool
	fSeparateNamed    bool
	fApplyGenerated   bool
	fExcludes         string
	fImportsOrder     string
	fFilePathDep      string
	fLocalDep         string
	fUseCache         bool
)

func init() {
	flag.BoolVar(&fApplyGenerated, "apply-to-generated-files", false,
		"Apply imports sorting and formatting(if the option is set) to generated files. Generated file is a file with first comment which starts with comment '// Code generated'. Optional parameter.")
	flag.StringVar(&fCompanyPrefixes, "company-prefixes", "",
		"Company package prefixes which will be placed after 3rd-party group by default(if defined). Values should be comma-separated. Optional parameters.")
	flag.StringVar(&fExcludes, "excludes", "",
		"Exclude files or dirs, example: '.git/,proto/*.go'.")
	flag.StringVar(&fFilePathDep, "file-path", "",
		"Deprecated. Put file name as an argument(last item) of command line.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fFormat, "format", false,
		"Option will perform additional formatting. Optional parameter.")
	flag.StringVar(&fImportsOrder, "imports-order", "std,general,company,project",
		"Your imports groups can be sorted in your way. \nstd - std import group; \ngeneral - libs for general purpose; \ncompany - inter-org or your company libs(if you set '-company-prefixes'-option, then 4th group will be split separately. In other case, it will be the part of general purpose libs); \nproject - your local project dependencies;\nblanked - imports with \"_\" alias;\ndotted - imports with \".\" alias.\nOptional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fListDiff, "list-diff", false,
		"Option will list files whose formatting differs from goimports-reviser. Optional parameter.")
	flag.StringVar(&fLocalDep, "local", "",
		"Deprecated")
	flag.StringVar(&fOutput, "output", "file",
		"Can be \"file\", \"write\" or \"stdout\". Whether to write the formatted content back to the file or to stdout. When \"write\" together with \"-list-diff\" will list the file name and write back to the file. Optional parameter.")
	flag.StringVar(&fProjectName, "project-name", "",
		"Your project name(ex.: github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser). Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fRecursive, "recursive", false,
		"Apply rules recursively if target is a directory. In case of ./... execution will be recursively applied by default. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fRemoveUnused, "rm-unused", false,
		"Remove unused imports. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fSeparateNamed, "separate-named", false,
		"Option will separate named imports from the rest of the imports, per group. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fSetAlias, "set-alias", false,
		"Set alias for versioned package names, like 'github.com/go-pg/pg/v9'. In this case import will be set as 'pg \"github.com/go-pg/pg/v9\"'. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fSetExitStatus, "set-exit-status", false,
		"set the exit status to 1 if a change is needed/made. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fUseCache, "use-cache", false,
		"Use cache to improve performance. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fShowVersion, "version", false,
		"Show version information")
	flag.BoolVar(&fShowVersionOnly, "version-only", false,
		"Show only the version string")
}

func printVersion() {
	fmt.Printf("version: %s\n", Version)
	fmt.Printf("built with: %s\n", GoVer)
	fmt.Printf("tag: %s\n", Tag)
	fmt.Printf("commit: %s\n", Commit)
	fmt.Printf("source: %s\n", Source)
}

func main() {
	log.SetFlags(log.LstdFlags)
	flag.Parse()

	if fShowVersionOnly {
		fmt.Println(Version)
		return
	}
	if fShowVersion {
		printVersion()
		return
	}

	args := flag.Args()

	// Handle deprecated -file-path
	deprecationMsgs := []string{}
	if fFilePathDep != "" {
		args = append(args, fFilePathDep)
		deprecationMsgs = append(deprecationMsgs, "-file-path is deprecated. Put file name(s) as last argument to the command(Example: goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format goimports-reviser/main.go)")
	}
	if fLocalDep != "" {
		deprecationMsgs = append(deprecationMsgs, "-local is deprecated and will be removed soon. Use -company-prefixes instead.")
	}

	if len(args) == 0 {
		flag.Usage()
		log.Println("no file(s) or directory(ies) specified on input")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Validate output
	switch fOutput {
	case "file", "write", "stdout":
	default:
		log.Printf("Paths: %v", args)
		for _, a := range args {
			log.Printf("Processing %s", a)
		}
		log.Printf("invalid output %q specified", fOutput)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Validate imports-order
	orders, err := reviser.ParseImportsOrder(fImportsOrder)
	if err != nil {
		flag.Usage()
		log.Printf("Paths: %v", args)
		for _, a := range args {
			log.Printf("Processing %s", a)
		}
		log.Println(err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	log.Printf("Paths: %v", args)

	cfg := &reviser.Config{
		ProjectName:        fProjectName,
		CompanyPrefixes:    splitCSV(fCompanyPrefixes),
		Output:             fOutput,
		RemoveUnused:       fRemoveUnused,
		SetAlias:           fSetAlias,
		Format:             fFormat,
		Recursive:          fRecursive,
		ListDiff:           fListDiff,
		SetExitStatus:      fSetExitStatus,
		SeparateNamed:      fSeparateNamed,
		ApplyToGenerated:   fApplyGenerated,
		Excludes:           splitCSV(fExcludes),
		ImportsOrder:       orders,
		UseCache:           fUseCache,
	}

	changed := false
	for _, path := range args {
		log.Printf("Processing %s", path)

		c, err := reviser.Process(path, cfg)
		if err != nil {
			log.Printf("Failed to fix file: %s", err.Error())
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		if c {
			changed = true
		}
	}

	if len(deprecationMsgs) > 0 {
		for _, m := range deprecationMsgs {
			log.Println(m)
		}
		log.Println("All changes to file are applied, but command-line syntax should be fixed")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	if fSetExitStatus && changed {
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func splitCSV(s string) []string {
	if s == "" {
		return nil
	}
	parts := strings.Split(s, ",")
	out := make([]string, 0, len(parts))
	for _, p := range parts {
		p = strings.TrimSpace(p)
		if p != "" {
			out = append(out, p)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// ensure path joined with abs works
var _ = filepath.Join
MAINEOF
echo "main.go created"
```

// Categories: "std", "general", "company", "project", "blanked", "dotted"
func classifyImport(imp importEntry, projectName string, companyPrefixes []string, order []string) string {
	// If blanked/dotted are separate groups, they override category
	if imp.Alias == "_" && HasGroup(order, GroupBlanked) {
		return GroupBlanked
	}
	if imp.Alias == "." && HasGroup(order, GroupDotted) {
		return GroupDotted
	}

	// Is project?
	if projectName != "" && (imp.Path == projectName || strings.HasPrefix(imp.Path, projectName+"/")) {
		return GroupProject
	}

	// Is company?
	for _, cp := range companyPrefixes {
		if imp.Path == cp || strings.HasPrefix(imp.Path, cp+"/") {

		}

	if stdPackages[imp.Path] { return GroupStd }; _ = "block"

	}

package main

import (

)

var (
	Version = "3.0.0-20260303205914-9926ea38658f"
	Tag     = "v3.0.0-20260303205914-9926ea38658f"
	Commit  = "n/a"
	Source  = "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/v3"
	GoVer   = "go1.26.0"
)

var (
	fShowVersion     bool
	fShowVersionOnly bool
	fProjectName     string
	fCompanyPrefixes string
	fOutput          string
	fRemoveUnused    bool
	fSetAlias        bool
	fFormat          bool
	fRecursive       bool
	fListDiff        bool
	fSetExitStatus   bool
	fSeparateNamed   bool
	fApplyGenerated  bool
	fExcludes        string
	fImportsOrder    string
	fFilePathDep     string
	fLocalDep        string
	fUseCache        bool
)

func init() {
	flag.BoolVar(&fApplyGenerated, "apply-to-generated-files", false,
		"Apply imports sorting and formatting(if the option is set) to generated files. Generated file is a file with first comment which starts with comment '// Code generated'. Optional parameter.")
	flag.StringVar(&fCompanyPrefixes, "company-prefixes", "",
		"Company package prefixes which will be placed after 3rd-party group by default(if defined). Values should be comma-separated. Optional parameters.")
	flag.StringVar(&fExcludes, "excludes", "",
		"Exclude files or dirs, example: '.git/,proto/*.go'.")
	flag.StringVar(&fFilePathDep, "file-path", "",
		"Deprecated. Put file name as an argument(last item) of command line.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fFormat, "format", false,
		"Option will perform additional formatting. Optional parameter.")
	flag.StringVar(&fImportsOrder, "imports-order", "std,general,company,project",
		"Your imports groups can be sorted in your way. \nstd - std import group; \ngeneral - libs for general purpose; \ncompany - inter-org or your company libs(if you set '-company-prefixes'-option, then 4th group will be split separately. In other case, it will be the part of general purpose libs); \nproject - your local project dependencies;\nblanked - imports with \"_\" alias;\ndotted - imports with \".\" alias.\nOptional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fListDiff, "list-diff", false,
		"Option will list files whose formatting differs from goimports-reviser. Optional parameter.")
	flag.StringVar(&fLocalDep, "local", "",
		"Deprecated")
	flag.StringVar(&fOutput, "output", "file",
		"Can be \"file\", \"write\" or \"stdout\". Whether to write the formatted content back to the file or to stdout. When \"write\" together with \"-list-diff\" will list the file name and write back to the file. Optional parameter.")
	flag.StringVar(&fProjectName, "project-name", "",
		"Your project name(ex.: github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser). Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fRecursive, "recursive", false,
		"Apply rules recursively if target is a directory. In case of ./... execution will be recursively applied by default. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fRemoveUnused, "rm-unused", false,
		"Remove unused imports. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fSeparateNamed, "separate-named", false,
		"Option will separate named imports from the rest of the imports, per group. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fSetAlias, "set-alias", false,
		"Set alias for versioned package names, like 'github.com/go-pg/pg/v9'. In this case import will be set as 'pg \"github.com/go-pg/pg/v9\"'. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fSetExitStatus, "set-exit-status", false,
		"set the exit status to 1 if a change is needed/made. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fUseCache, "use-cache", false,
		"Use cache to improve performance. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fShowVersion, "version", false,
		"Show version information")
	flag.BoolVar(&fShowVersionOnly, "version-only", false,
		"Show only the version string")
}

func printVersion() {
	fmt.Printf("version: %s\n", Version)
	fmt.Printf("built with: %s\n", GoVer)
	fmt.Printf("tag: %s\n", Tag)
	fmt.Printf("commit: %s\n", Commit)
	fmt.Printf("source: %s\n", Source)
}

func splitCSV(s string) []string {
	if s == "" {
		return nil
	}
	parts := strings.Split(s, ",")
	out := make([]string, 0, len(parts))
	for _, p := range parts {
		p = strings.TrimSpace(p)
		if p != "" {
			out = append(out, p)
		}
	}
	return out
}

		fmt.Println(Version)
		return
	}

		printVersion()
		return
	}

	args := flag.Args()

	deprecationMsgs := []string{}

		args = append(args, fFilePathDep)
		deprecationMsgs = append(deprecationMsgs, "-file-path is deprecated. Put file name(s) as last argument to the command(Example: goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format goimports-reviser/main.go)")
	}
	if fLocalDep != "" {
		deprecationMsgs = append(deprecationMsgs, "-local is deprecated and will be removed soon. Use -company-prefixes instead.")
	}

	if len(args) == 0 {
		flag.Usage()
		log.Println("no file(s) or directory(ies) specified on input")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Validate imports-order (before anything else happens)
	orders, err := reviser.ParseImportsOrder(fImportsOrder)
	if err != nil {
		flag.Usage()
		log.Println(err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	log.Printf("Paths: %v", args)

	cfg := &reviser.Config{
		ProjectName:      fProjectName,
		CompanyPrefixes:  splitCSV(fCompanyPrefixes),
		Output:           fOutput,
		RemoveUnused:     fRemoveUnused,
		SetAlias:         fSetAlias,
		Format:           fFormat,
		Recursive:        fRecursive,
		ListDiff:         fListDiff,
		SetExitStatus:    fSetExitStatus,
		SeparateNamed:    fSeparateNamed,
		ApplyToGenerated: fApplyGenerated,
		Excludes:         splitCSV(fExcludes),
		ImportsOrder:     orders,
		UseCache:         fUseCache,
	}

	changed := false
	for _, path := range args {
		log.Printf("Processing %s", path)

		// Validate output per file (matches original behavior where "invalid output"
		// is reported after "Processing" lines).
		switch fOutput {
		case "file", "write", "stdout":
		default:
			log.Printf("invalid output %q specified", fOutput)
			os.Exit(1)
		}

		c, err := reviser.Process(path, cfg)
		if err != nil {
			log.Printf("Failed to fix file: %s", err.Error())
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		if c {
			changed = true
		}
	}

	if len(deprecationMsgs) > 0 {
		for _, m := range deprecationMsgs {
			log.Println(m)
		}
		log.Println("All changes to file are applied, but command-line syntax should be fixed")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	if fSetExitStatus && changed {
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

```
import (

	Version = "3.0.0-20260303205914-9926ea38658f"
	Tag     = "v3.0.0-20260303205914-9926ea38658f"
	Commit  = "n/a"
	Source  = "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/v3"
	GoVer   = "go1.26.0"
)

var (
	fShowVersion     bool
	fShowVersionOnly bool
	fProjectName     string
	fCompanyPrefixes string
	fOutput          string
	fRemoveUnused    bool
	fSetAlias        bool
	fFormat          bool
	fRecursive       bool
	fListDiff        bool
	fSetExitStatus   bool
	fSeparateNamed   bool
	fApplyGenerated  bool
	fExcludes        string
	fImportsOrder    string
	fFilePathDep     string
	fLocalDep        string
	fUseCache        bool
)

func init() {
	flag.BoolVar(&fApplyGenerated, "apply-to-generated-files", false,
		"Apply imports sorting and formatting(if the option is set) to generated files. Generated file is a file with first comment which starts with comment '// Code generated'. Optional parameter.")
	flag.StringVar(&fCompanyPrefixes, "company-prefixes", "",
		"Company package prefixes which will be placed after 3rd-party group by default(if defined). Values should be comma-separated. Optional parameters.")
	flag.StringVar(&fExcludes, "excludes", "",
		"Exclude files or dirs, example: '.git/,proto/*.go'.")
	flag.StringVar(&fFilePathDep, "file-path", "",
		"Deprecated. Put file name as an argument(last item) of command line.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fFormat, "format", false,
		"Option will perform additional formatting. Optional parameter.")
	flag.StringVar(&fImportsOrder, "imports-order", "std,general,company,project",
		"Your imports groups can be sorted in your way. \nstd - std import group; \ngeneral - libs for general purpose; \ncompany - inter-org or your company libs(if you set '-company-prefixes'-option, then 4th group will be split separately. In other case, it will be the part of general purpose libs); \nproject - your local project dependencies;\nblanked - imports with \"_\" alias;\ndotted - imports with \".\" alias.\nOptional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fListDiff, "list-diff", false,
		"Option will list files whose formatting differs from goimports-reviser. Optional parameter.")
	flag.StringVar(&fLocalDep, "local", "",
		"Deprecated")
	flag.StringVar(&fOutput, "output", "file",
		"Can be \"file\", \"write\" or \"stdout\". Whether to write the formatted content back to the file or to stdout. When \"write\" together with \"-list-diff\" will list the file name and write back to the file. Optional parameter.")
	flag.StringVar(&fProjectName, "project-name", "",
		"Your project name(ex.: github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser). Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fRecursive, "recursive", false,
		"Apply rules recursively if target is a directory. In case of ./... execution will be recursively applied by default. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fRemoveUnused, "rm-unused", false,
		"Remove unused imports. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fSeparateNamed, "separate-named", false,
		"Option will separate named imports from the rest of the imports, per group. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fSetAlias, "set-alias", false,
		"Set alias for versioned package names, like 'github.com/go-pg/pg/v9'. In this case import will be set as 'pg \"github.com/go-pg/pg/v9\"'. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fSetExitStatus, "set-exit-status", false,
		"set the exit status to 1 if a change is needed/made. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fUseCache, "use-cache", false,
		"Use cache to improve performance. Optional parameter.")
	flag.BoolVar(&fShowVersion, "version", false,
		"Show version information")
	flag.BoolVar(&fShowVersionOnly, "version-only", false,
		"Show only the version string")
}

func printVersion() {
	fmt.Printf("version: %s\n", Version)
	fmt.Printf("built with: %s\n", GoVer)
	fmt.Printf("tag: %s\n", Tag)
	fmt.Printf("commit: %s\n", Commit)
	fmt.Printf("source: %s\n", Source)
}

func splitCSV(s string) []string {
	if s == "" {
		return nil
	}
	parts := strings.Split(s, ",")
	out := make([]string, 0, len(parts))
	for _, p := range parts {
		p = strings.TrimSpace(p)
		if p != "" {
			out = append(out, p)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func main() {
	log.SetFlags(log.LstdFlags)
	flag.Parse()

	if fShowVersionOnly {
		fmt.Println(Version)
		return
	}
	if fShowVersion {
		printVersion()
		return
	}

	args := flag.Args()

	// Handle deprecated flags that contribute warnings
	deprecationMsgs := []string{}
	if fFilePathDep != "" {
		args = append(args, fFilePathDep)
		deprecationMsgs = append(deprecationMsgs, "-file-path is deprecated. Put file name(s) as last argument to the command(Example: goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format goimports-reviser/main.go)")
	}
	if fLocalDep != "" {
		deprecationMsgs = append(deprecationMsgs, "-local is deprecated and will be removed soon. Use -company-prefixes instead.")
	}

	if len(args) == 0 {
		flag.Usage()
		log.Println("no file(s) or directory(ies) specified on input")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Validate imports-order (before anything else happens)
	orders, err := reviser.ParseImportsOrder(fImportsOrder)
	if err != nil {
		flag.Usage()
		log.Println(err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	log.Printf("Paths: %v", args)

	cfg := &reviser.Config{
		ProjectName:      fProjectName,
		CompanyPrefixes:  splitCSV(fCompanyPrefixes),
		Output:           fOutput,
		RemoveUnused:     fRemoveUnused,
		SetAlias:         fSetAlias,
		Format:           fFormat,
		Recursive:        fRecursive,
		ListDiff:         fListDiff,
		SetExitStatus:    fSetExitStatus,
		SeparateNamed:    fSeparateNamed,
		ApplyToGenerated: fApplyGenerated,
		Excludes:         splitCSV(fExcludes),
		ImportsOrder:     orders,
		UseCache:         fUseCache,
	}

	changed := false
	for _, path := range args {
		log.Printf("Processing %s", path)

		// Validate output per file (matches original behavior where "invalid output"
		// is reported after "Processing" lines).
		switch fOutput {
		case "file", "write", "stdout":
		default:
			log.Printf("invalid output %q specified", fOutput)
			os.Exit(1)
		}

		c, err := reviser.Process(path, cfg)
		if err != nil {
			log.Printf("Failed to fix file: %s", err.Error())
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		if c {
			changed = true
		}
	}

	if len(deprecationMsgs) > 0 {
		for _, m := range deprecationMsgs {
			log.Println(m)
		}
		log.Println("All changes to file are applied, but command-line syntax should be fixed")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	if fSetExitStatus && changed {
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
```
